context_requirements: Bacterial cells for canonical antibacterial activity; human cell lines lack the bacterial targets of most antibacterials
For DNMT1-directed compounds, DNMT1 expression and active DNA methylation maintenance
Sufficient intracellular drug exposure at 10 micromolar in human cells
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in multiple human cell lines
Consistent DNMT1 target engagement signatures such as DNA methylation-dependent gene reactivation
Shared transcriptional response across the nine lines that is not explained by generic stress or cytotoxicity

evidence.supports: Triclosan, an antibacterial agent, altered DNA methylation and gene expression in zebrafish, suggesting possible epigenetic effects
Triclosan altered endocrine-related and heat shock gene transcription in aquatic larvae
Ofloxacin induced time-dependent stress, inflammatory, and proteolysis gene expression changes in rat cartilage
